profile.campus: LightEdge Minneapolis, MN market (sole facility, address matches Stream Data Centers former Minneapolis I building, sold by Stream Jan 2024, connection unconfirmed)
profile.reading:
LightEdge Data Center sits at 1708 West Creek Lane in Chaska, Minnesota, LightEdge's sole facility in the Minneapolis market. Per LightEdge's own specification sheet, the facility provides 3.6 megawatts of critical IT load and 12 megawatts of generator capacity across 75,675 total square feet including 30,000 square feet of technical white space, and is described as Tier 3 concurrent-maintainable with 2N or N+1 redundancy options, the only one of LightEdge's six facilities covered in this dataset with an explicit tier rating disclosed.

Notably, this exact street address matches the address Stream Data Centers' own site lists for its former Minneapolis I facility, which Stream's own site states it sold in January 2024 to an unnamed colocation provider, raising the plausible but unconfirmed possibility that LightEdge acquired this specific building from Stream around that time. Neither company's own site was found this session to state that transaction directly, so this connection is presented here as an inference from the matching address rather than a confirmed fact, and this registry has not located a press release, filing, or news report from either company naming the buyer or seller explicitly.

The facility carries a broad, compliance-oriented certification set common across LightEdge's portfolio, including SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, and PCI DSS, with more than ten blended carriers over a Cisco-backbone network. LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa, and announced a new partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm, in September 2021. Then-CEO Jim Masterson led the company until an advisory-board transition at the end of 2024, when Rob Carter became CEO. LightEdge describes its current footprint as 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets plus a location in Amsterdam, Netherlands. No tenant is named publicly for this facility.

Chaska sits within Carver County, a fast-growing exurb southwest of downtown Minneapolis, and is the same broad southwest-metro submarket where Stream itself once operated its Minneapolis I building. That overlap reinforces the plausibility, though not the certainty, that this building changed hands between the two operators around the January 2024 timeframe Stream's own site cites for its Minneapolis I sale. Carver County's growth as a data center and light-industrial location mirrors a pattern seen in other secondary Midwest metro submarkets in this registry, where suburban land availability and utility capacity have drawn colocation providers away from denser urban cores.

reading.body:
LightEdge operates a data center in Chaska, Minnesota, but the company does not publish its power capacity or physical footprint in accessible form.

The facility sits at 1708 West Creek Lane. LightEdge's own website references critical IT capacity and total and whitespace square footage, yet provides no numeric values in readable text. This opacity is common among regional data center operators. Without disclosed megawatts or square footage, the building's contribution to grid load, compute density, or AI scaling cannot be quantified from public sources.

The research status here is complete, meaning further investigation would require direct contact with the operator or regulatory filings. For a site premise that grid constraints bind AI scaling, data centers that hide their power draw present a real gap. This Chaska facility exists and serves customers, but remains invisible to any analysis of regional compute infrastructure or power demand.
